name: Concatenating Strings and Numbers (Case 2)
description: Construct a program that uses variables x, y, and z to print "x * 2 = 4".
code:
#Step 1: Assign initial values to the variables x, y, and z
x = 2
y = "x * 2 = "
z = x * 2
#Step 2: Print the text using the variables initialized above 
print(y + str(z))

1.content: #Step 1: Assign initial values to the variables x, y, and z

commentList: This statement sets variable x to the integer 2.
This statement sets variable y to the string "x * 2 = ".
This statement sets variable z to the integer value that is the result of the multiplication operation.

The expression on the right-hand side of the assignment operator multiplies the value stored in variable x by 2. The result of the multiplication is an integer value because both operands of the multiplication operator are integers. Note that variable x has an integer value.

5.content: #Step 2: Print the text using the variables initialized above

commentList: This statement concatenates the content of variables y, z to print the requested output. We concatenate the content of these variables using the + operator. Variable y has a string value and we can use the + operator to concatenate its content with any other string. Variable z, on the other hand, has an integer value and its value can be concatenated with a string only when we it is explicitly converted to a string using the str function.
Note that the concatenating and printing are done in the same line. That is, we don't have to store the concatenated string to a new variable at first and then print it in the next line.
Note that the + operator creates a new string from the contents of its operands joined. This string will be printed by the print function and followed by the end-of-line character at the end.
